root_cause.text: The `match_char()` macro evaluates its argument multiple times, so when invoked with an expression containing a side effect like `*str++`, the pointer increment occurs multiple times per logical character, causing characters to be skipped and leading to out-of-bounds reads.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states: "The match_char() macro evaluates its character parameter multiple times when traversing differential encoding chains. When invoked with *str++, the string pointer advances on each iteration of the inner do-while loop, causing the DFA to check different characters at each iteration and therefore skip input characters. This results in out-of-bounds reads..." The patch fixes this by extracting the character value before invoking `match_char`, ensuring single evaluation per outer loop iteration.
